title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Concealing Physical Evidence
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client comes to their paralegal's office, places a bloody knife on the desk, and admits it was used in an assault. The client asks the paralegal to keep it in their safe. Does the paralegal's duty of confidentiality protect this physical evidence?
options: Yes, physical evidence handed over by a client falls under absolute solicitor-client privilege.
Yes, the paralegal must keep the item safe to prevent it from falling into police hands.
No, the duty of confidentiality applies to information, not to the concealment or destruction of physical evidence of a crime.
No, but the paralegal is permitted to wipe the fingerprints off before returning it to the client.
questions.explain: Ethical guidelines are clear: while a practitioner must hold client *communications* and *information* in strict confidence, they cannot become an active participant in concealing, destroying, or altering physical evidence of a crime. Taking possession of a murder weapon/instrument of crime creates an obligation to surrender it to authorities, creating a severe conflict, and the paralegal should refuse to take possession of it.
